{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = 'data/sales.csv'
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Clean the revenue column: remove commas and convert to float
data['revenue_clean'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Remove QA orders (revenue == 999999.99) and refunded orders
data_filtered = data[(data['revenue_clean'] != 999999.99) & (data['status'] == 'completed')]

# Check the number of rows after filtering
print(f"Number of completed, non-QA orders: {len(data_filtered)}")

# Now check for confounding: is `channel` associated with `customer_segment`?
print("Cross-tabulation of channel vs customer_segment:")
print(pd.crosstab(data_filtered['channel'], data_filtered['customer_segment']))

# Check conversion rate by channel
print("Conversion rate by channel:")
conversion_by_channel = data_filtered.groupby('channel')['converted'].mean()
print(conversion_by_channel)

# Check if customer_segment is associated with conversion
print("Conversion rate by customer_segment:")
conversion_by_segment = data_filtered.groupby('customer_segment')['converted'].mean()
print(conversion_by_segment)

# Also check revenue by channel (to assess campaign success)
print("Average revenue by channel:")
revenue_by_channel = data_filtered.groupby('channel')['revenue_clean'].mean()
print(revenue_by_channel)

# Check if customer_segment is associated with revenue
print("Average revenue by customer_segment:")
revenue_by_segment = data_filtered.groupby('customer_segment')['revenue_clean'].mean()
print(revenue_by_segment)"}
